raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On an fp8 KV cache, `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` divides `cache_k` / `cache_v` by the KV scales **in place**. Two callers pay for that contract when they don't need to:

1. **`TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend`** reads `k` / `v` again in the attention kernel after the KV write, so on the scaled path it clones both before the write (`k.clone(),  # cloned to protect k,v from in-place mutation in set_kv_buffer`). The MLA sub-branch does the same with `k.clone().div_(layer.k_scale)`. As a result, every scaled prefill write runs a full extra copy of K and V.
2. **`HybridLinearKVPool`, `SWAKVPool` and `UnifiedSWAKVPool`** default `k_scale` / `v_scale` to `1.0` in `set_kv_buffer`, while `MHATokenToKVPool` defaults them to `None`. When a caller writes without a scale (QSA, MiniMax-M3's sparse layers through `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, or triton on an unquantized model), the wrapper substitutes `1.0` and the MHA pool runs a full `div_(1.0)` over K and V. That is a pass over HBM that changes nothing.

This PR removes both. The bytes written to the KV cache are unchanged.

Making the pool itself out of place (`cache_k = cache_k / k_scale`) looks like the obvious fix but measures worse, so it is not what this PR does:
- Every caller that never needed protection would pay a new allocation, and that includes every triton decode step.
- `AiterAttnBackend` hands the pool a shape-`[1]` fp32 unit scale. With that scale, an out-of-place divide promotes bf16 to fp32 (a 0-dim scale would not).
- Measured on the micro below, that variant is −3.6 % (median) on the unprotected callers and −9.7 % (down to −33 %) on the aiter path.

## Modifications

- `triton_backend.py`, `forward_extend`: on the scaled MHA path, divide out of place (`k / layer.k_scale`, `v / layer.v_scale`) and pass the pool no scale. On the MLA sub-branch, `k / layer.k_scale` replaces `k.clone().div_(...)`. In both cases one divide replaces clone + divide. `layer.k_scale` is the 0-dim fp32 parameter `BaseKVCacheMethod` creates, so the result stays bf16 and is bit-identical to the pool's in-place divide.
- `HybridLinearKVPool.set_kv_buffer`, `SWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer`, `UnifiedSWAKVPool.set_kv_buffer`: change the `k_scale` / `v_scale` defaults from `1.0` to `None`.
  - Every pool these wrappers forward to treats `None` as "no divide": `MHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolFP4`, `PageInterleaveMHATokenToKVPool` and the NPU pool all guard with `if k_scale is not None`.
  - `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8` treats `None` as its fused quant-store signal. Its only caller passes the scales explicitly (`flashattention_backend`), so the default never reached it.
  - Callers that pass a scale explicitly are unaffected.
- New CPU unit test, `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_write_scale_contract.py`.

`MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer`'s own semantics are untouched. #31652 (fused fp8 store, CUDA) and #40785 (fused prefix-valid commit) do not overlap this diff textually.

## Accuracy Tests

The values written to the KV cache are bit-identical:
- In the micro below, the sha1 of the fp8 bytes written into the pool matches `main` at every shape, token count and path.
- The unit test asserts the pool receives exactly `k.clone().div_(layer.k_scale)`, same dtype and same values.

No model-level accuracy run yet (see below).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm image with torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0. Measured on `main@ef867fa40d`; none of the touched files or `kv_cache.py` / `radix_attention.py` has changed between that commit and this branch's base.

The micro times the real `TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend` KV-save block and the real `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer` on an `fp8_e4m3` pool, with K/V given as contiguous views of one fused QKV buffer. Run design:
- Shapes are kv_heads × head_dim × q_heads: 2×256×16 (Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5), 4×128×64 (MiniMax-M3) and 8×128×48 (MiniMax-M2.7).
- Token counts are 37 / 509 / 2053 / 6151 / 30727.
- Each arm (base, this PR, and the pool-out-of-place alternative) is one consecutive block of 4 runs. Run 1 is discarded and runs 2–4 are medianed.
- Timing is device time: one call captured in a CUDA graph and replayed.

Median over the 15 shape × token points, with the range in brackets; positive means faster:

| path | who takes it | this PR | pool out-of-place (rejected) |
|---|---|---|---|
| scaled triton extend write | `--attention-backend triton` + fp8 KV + quantized attention | **+36.4 %** [+9.5, +41.4] | +35.6 % |
| same, behind `HybridLinearKVPool` | Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 on triton | **+36.9 %** [+9.8, +40.9] | +36.0 % |
| unscaled write through a wrapper | QSA (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), MiniMax-M3 sparse layers, unquantized hybrids on triton | **+53.4 %** [+42.1, +72.9] | −0.6 % |
| pool write with a 0-dim scale, no caller clone | triton decode, FA / flashinfer / hpc / xpu | −0.1 % [−0.6, +1.9] | −3.6 % [−10.7, −0.7] |
| pool write with aiter's `[1]` unit scale | aiter's non-fused branch (SWA pools) | 0.0 % | −9.7 % [−33.1, +1.7] |

Selected points (µs, device time):

| point | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| triton extend, 2×256×16, 509 tok | 24.44 | 17.69 | +38.1 % |
| triton extend, 2×256×16, 30727 tok | 136.63 | 115.86 | +17.9 % |
| triton extend, 8×128×48, 6151 tok | 69.52 | 58.83 | +18.2 % |
| wrapper unscaled, 2×256×16, 509 tok | 15.10 | 10.29 | +46.8 % |
| wrapper unscaled, 2×256×16, 30727 tok | 54.96 | 32.60 | +68.6 % |

Wall-clock time (Python and launch overhead included) gives +17–18 % on the triton extend write at ≥ 6151 tokens. The ordering is the same on every other path.

**Which models reach it.** Probed with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, truncated dummy-weight checkpoints, under both the ROCm default backend and `--attention-backend triton`. FP8 KV is opt-in for all of these.

| model | ROCm default backend | `--attention-backend triton` |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-Next-80B-FP8, Qwen3.5-397B-MXFP4, Qwen3.8-2.4T-MXFP4, MiniMax-M2.7 | aiter fused write, not reached | scaled extend write (full-attention layers) |
| MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 (text-only config) | default is triton: scaled extend write on dense layers, wrapper unscaled write on sparse layers | same |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 | QSA: wrapper unscaled write | same |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (bf16 weights) | aiter fused, not reached | wrapper unscaled write |
| Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-14B-FP8 (controls) | aiter fused | `scale=None`, not reached |
| DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3, Kimi-Linear, gpt-oss | 0 hits (own MLA/DSA pools, or the model fuses its KV write) | 0 hits |

**Not done yet (why this is a draft):** an end-to-end serving A/B and a GSM8K A/B with a base-repeat control. The planned runs are Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 on the default backend for the wrapper path, and Qwen3-Next-80B-FP8 with `--attention-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` for the extend path. The micro numbers above are per KV write; the end-to-end share depends on how much of a step those writes take.

**Unit test.** `test_kv_write_scale_contract.py` is CPU-only and run from outside the repo, so it imports the tree under test:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 6 failed (all wrapper cases, plus the triton pre-scaled-write case) |
| this PR's triton change alone (wrapper defaults left at 1.0) | 5 failed (wrapper cases) |
| pool made out-of-place instead | 6 failed |
| this PR | 4 passed, 10 subtests passed |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (micro done; e2e and GSM8K pending)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -0,0 +1,153 @@
+"""Unit tests for how KV-cache scales reach MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer.
+
+The pool divides cache_k / cache_v by the scales it is given in place, so a caller
+that reads K/V after the write must scale out of place and hand the pool no scale,
+and a wrapper pool must not substitute a scale when its caller passed none.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.triton_backend import TritonAttnBackend
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import HybridLinearKVPool, KVWriteLoc
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.swa_memory_pool import SWAKVPool
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_memory_pool import UnifiedSWAKVPool
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+NUM_TOKENS, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, Q_HEADS = 37, 2, 64, 8
+
+
+class _Stop(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class _RecordingPool:
+    def __init__(self, stop_after_write=False):
+        self.calls = []
+        self.stop_after_write = stop_after_write
+
+    def set_kv_buffer(
+        self, layer, loc, cache_k, cache_v, k_scale=None, v_scale=None, **kwargs
+    ):
+        self.calls.append(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                cache_k=cache_k.clone(),
+                cache_v=cache_v.clone(),
+                k_scale=k_scale,
+                v_scale=v_scale,
+            )
+        )
+        if self.stop_after_write:
+            raise _Stop
+
+
+def _make_kv():
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    # Contiguous views into one fused buffer, as the QKV projection hands them over.
+    kv = torch.randn(2 * NUM_TOKENS, KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, generator=g).bfloat16()
+    return kv[:NUM_TOKENS], kv[NUM_TOKENS:]
+
+
+def _wrapper_cases():
+    loc = torch.arange(NUM_TOKENS)
+    for cls in (SWAKVPool, UnifiedSWAKVPool):
+        for is_swa in (False, True):
+            full, swa = _RecordingPool(), _RecordingPool()
+            pool = SimpleNamespace(
+                full_kv_pool=full, swa_kv_pool=swa, layers_mapping={0: (0, is_swa)}
+            )
+            inner = swa if is_swa else full
+            yield (
+                f"{cls.__name__}(swa={is_swa})",
+                cls,
+                pool,
+                inner,
+                KVWriteLoc(loc, loc),
+            )
+    inner = _RecordingPool()
+    pool = SimpleNamespace(
+        full_kv_pool=inner,
+        use_mla=False,
+        _transfer_full_attention_id=lambda layer_id: layer_id,
+    )
+    yield "HybridLinearKVPool", HybridLinearKVPool, pool, inner, KVWriteLoc(loc)
+
+
+class TestWrapperPoolScaleForwarding(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_unscaled_write_stays_unscaled(self):
+        # A substituted 1.0 makes the MHA pool run a full div_ pass over K and V.
+        k, v = _make_kv()
+        for name, cls, pool, inner, loc in _wrapper_cases():
+            with self.subTest(pool=name):
+                cls.set_kv_buffer(pool, SimpleNamespace(layer_id=0), loc, k, v)
+                self.assertEqual(len(inner.calls), 1)
+                self.assertIsNone(inner.calls[0].k_scale)
+                self.assertIsNone(inner.calls[0].v_scale)
+
+    def test_explicit_scale_is_forwarded(self):
+        k, v = _make_kv()
+        k_scale, v_scale = torch.tensor(0.73), torch.tensor(0.61)
+        for name, cls, pool, inner, loc in _wrapper_cases():
+            with self.subTest(pool=name):
+                cls.set_kv_buffer(
+                    pool, SimpleNamespace(layer_id=0), loc, k, v, k_scale, v_scale
+                )
+                self.assertIs(inner.calls[0].k_scale, k_scale)
+                self.assertIs(inner.calls[0].v_scale, v_scale)
+
+
+class TestTritonExtendScaledKVWrite(CustomTestCase):
+    def _save_kv(self, use_mla):
+        k, v = _make_kv()
+        k_before, v_before = k.clone(), v.clone()
+        q = torch.randn(NUM_TOKENS, Q_HEADS * HEAD_DIM).bfloat16()
+        # 0-dim fp32 parameters, as BaseKVCacheMethod creates them.
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(
+            layer_id=0,
+            k_scale=torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.73), requires_grad=False),
+            v_scale=torch.nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.61), requires_grad=False),
+        )
+        pool = _RecordingPool(stop_after_write=True)
+        backend = object.__new__(TritonAttnBackend)
+        backend.use_dense_fp8_chunked_prefill = False
+        backend.dcp_size = 1
+        backend.use_mla = use_mla
+        backend.token_to_kv_pool = pool
+        backend.forward_metadata = SimpleNamespace(
+            custom_mask=None, swa_out_cache_loc=None, out_cache_loc_full_physical=None
+        )
+        forward_batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            out_cache_loc=torch.arange(NUM_TOKENS),
+            out_cache_loc_is_physical=False,
+            attn_attend_prefix_cache=None,
+            _attn_output=torch.empty_like(q),
+        )
+        with self.assertRaises(_Stop):
+            TritonAttnBackend.forward_extend(backend, q, k, v, layer, forward_batch)
+        # The attention kernel that runs after the write reads the caller's k / v.
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(k, k_before))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(v, v_before))
+        self.assertEqual(len(pool.calls), 1)
+        return pool.calls[0], k_before, v_before, layer
+
+    def test_mha_write_is_prescaled_and_unscaled_at_pool(self):
+        call, k, v, layer = self._save_kv(use_mla=False)
+        self.assertIsNone(call.k_scale)
+        self.assertIsNone(call.v_scale)
+        # Same values, same dtype as the pool's in-place divide would produce.
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(call.cache_k, k.clone().div_(layer.k_scale)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(call.cache_v, v.clone().div_(layer.v_scale)))
+
+    def test_mla_write_is_prescaled(self):
+        call, k, v, layer = self._save_kv(use_mla=True)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(call.cache_k, k.clone().div_(layer.k_scale)))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(call.cache_v, v))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
